rawFindings.title: stderr output is no longer captured for failed browser starts on supported Node versions
rawFindings.explanation: The new guard limits the stderr data handler to Node 0.8. For Node 0.10 and newer, a browser process that exists but exits non-zero after writing diagnostics to stderr will now call `_onProcessExit` with an empty `errorOutput`, because no stderr listener is registered.
rawFindings.suggestion: Register a stderr `data` listener unconditionally to append stderr to `errorOutput`, and keep only the Node 0.8 "No such file or directory" special-case inside the version check.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: On Node 0.10.x, if `/usr/bin/browser` starts, writes `invalid option --foo` to stderr, and exits with code 1, the launcher logs `Cannot start <browser>` with a blank diagnostic instead of including `invalid option --foo`.
